nodes.label: Project bootstrap: agent structure, functional requirements, GitHub setup, MVP issues and CLI skeleton (#1)
nodes.description:
Goal: set up the repo for agents, write the functional requirements with the user acting as client, publish the repo on GitHub and start the MVP.
Instructions: no commits/pushes without the user's confirmation; secrets only in .env, never printed; no gh CLI, use git + GitHub REST API with curl; conventions in CONTRIBUTING.md; rule 1 of AGENTS.md (read the skill first).
Discoveries: the user's success moment is asking impact questions ('what are the implications of changing X'); the token could create labels and milestones; pytest was not installed in env/ until pip install -e .[dev].
Accomplished: agent structure (AGENTS.md, .agents/skills, .agents/tools, .mcp.json); docs/requisitos-funcionales.md v1.0 approved (sections 9 and 10 closed); git repo initialised and pushed to private GitHub repo Cristian1A/kg (commit 7d4bd49); 19 labels, milestones v0.1 (MVP) and v0.2, 12 MVP issues (#1-#12); issue #1 implemented (package renamed to kg, argparse CLI skeleton, 21 new tests) and PR #13 opened.
Next steps: user reviews and merges PR #13; then issue #2 (JSON Schema with standard catalog), ideally branching from main after the merge; follow order #1 -> #2 -> #3/#4 -> #5 -> rest in parallel -> #12.
Relevant files: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, src/kg/cli.py, tests/test_cli.py, pyproject.toml, .env.example.

nodes.description:
What: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md v1.0 approved 2026-10-07 with ~40 RF-xx (MVP / v0.2 / Future), 9 RNF, 6 use cases, 5 MVP acceptance criteria; open questions closed: PA-01 name stays 'kg', PA-02 IDs are <type>:<slug>, PA-03 interactive HTML with pyvis (vis.js); assumptions S-01..S-03 accepted; proposed out-of-scope list (section 9) accepted as is.
Why: requirements gathered by an interview where the user played the client, in 4 blocks recorded in respuestas_usuario.txt.
Where: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md (sections 9 and 10).
Learned: the user's example questions became use cases CU-02..CU-04 and drive acceptance.

nodes.label: Success = answering impact questions like 'what changes if I change X'
nodes.description:
What: the user's success moment is asking the tool about the implications of changing a part of the project.
Why: it is the client's stated main need in the requirements interview (block 1).
Where: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md use cases.
Learned: this is the requirement that most shapes the design (CLI graph queries vs. an agent reading the graph and reasoning).

nodes.label: The LLM lives in the external agent; kg itself needs no API keys
nodes.description:
What: kg is a deterministic CLI used by humans and AI agents; any LLM reasoning or extraction is done by the calling agent, which feeds JSON to kg.
Why: keeps the tool free of API keys and providers; agreed in requirements block 4.
Where: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md; component agents (skill for extraction).
Learned: hence the need for a strict JSON schema with actionable validation errors.

nodes.label: Store the graph as JSON in a .kg/ folder versioned with git
nodes.description:
What: kg init creates a .kg/ directory with deterministic JSON files meant to be committed.
Why: diffable, reviewable, no database; recommended in block 4 and adopted in RF-70/RF-71.
Where: .kg/ store, issue #4.
Learned: determinism (stable ordering) is required for clean git diffs.

nodes.label: Hybrid schema: standard catalog plus free types, stable IDs and provenance
nodes.description:
What: entities and relations use a standard catalog but free types are allowed; every entity has a stable ID to avoid duplicates and every datum records its provenance.
Why: repos differ; a closed catalog is too rigid and a free one cannot be queried consistently.
Where: docs/requisitos-funcionales.md data model; issues #2, #3.
Learned: multi-source provenance and advanced dedup were left for v0.2.

nodes.label: Basic merge by ID moved into the MVP (RF-30)
nodes.description:
What: kg add merges nodes by ID already in v0.1.
Why: the user had not marked it for v0.1, but without it kg add and kg extract would create duplicate nodes.
Where: RF-30, issue #5.
Learned: multi-provenance and advanced dedup stay in v0.2; the post-commit hook was put in v0.2 because it depends on incremental update.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits (in Spanish) with Closes/RF footers, feat/N-slug branches, [area] issue titles
nodes.description:
What: commits 'type(scope): summary' in Spanish with footers 'Closes: #N' and 'RF: RF-xx'; scopes are modules (schema, extract, store, render...); branches like feat/3-json-schema; issue titles '[area] description'; issue templates feature/bug, PR template with pytest+ruff checklist; labels type:*, prio:mvp|v0.2|futuro, area:*, status:blocked; milestones v0.1 (MVP) and v0.2.
Why: link every change to an issue and a requirement; proposed by the assistant and accepted by the user.
Where: CONTRIBUTING.md, .gitmessage, .github/ templates, AGENTS.md rule 9.
Learned: GitHub default labels (bug, enhancement...) were left in place pending the user's call.

nodes.label: No gh CLI: push with git, GitHub operations via REST API with the token from .env
nodes.description:
What: gh is not installed; pushes use git and issues/labels/PRs use curl against the GitHub REST API; the fine-grained token (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO) lives in .env (mode 600, gitignored), is loaded only for the operation and never printed; the origin remote URL does not contain the token.
Why: keep the secret out of the chat, .git/config and history (AGENTS.md rule 10).
Where: .env, .env.example, repo github.com/Cristian1A/kg (private).
Learned: the token turned out to have enough permission to create labels and milestones too.

nodes.label: No commits, pushes or file deletions without the user's confirmation
nodes.description:
What: the assistant prepares changes and asks before committing, pushing, opening PRs or deleting files; merges are left to the user unless asked (squash/merge/rebase to be chosen).
Why: AGENTS.md rule; the user wants control over history.
Where: AGENTS.md.
Learned: also verify before each commit that .env, env/ and local instruction files are not staged.

nodes.label: Deliver the v0.1 MVP: issues #1-#12 in dependency order
nodes.description:
What: 12 MVP issues: #1 CLI skeleton, #2 JSON Schema, #3 kg validate, #4 kg init/.kg, #5 kg add with ID merge, #6 extract Python structure, #7 extract deps/config, #8 extract tests, #9 render PNG/SVG, #10 render HTML pyvis, #11 agent extraction skill, #12 MVP validation on 3 repos.
Why: derived from the MVP RF-xx of the approved requirements.
Where: GitHub milestone v0.1 (MVP).
Learned: order #1 -> #2 -> #3 and #4 in parallel -> #5 -> extraction (#6-#8), render (#9, #10) and skill (#11) in parallel -> #12 closes the milestone.

nodes.label: Issue #1: kg package and base CLI (PR #13 awaiting merge)
nodes.description:
What: package renamed networkx_project -> kg with git mv; argparse CLI with stub subcommands init/extract/add/validate/render; --json and --kg-dir accepted before or after the subcommand; 21 tests in tests/test_cli.py; commit 42067c5 on feat/1-cli-base, PR #13 opened to main.
Why: base for every other MVP issue.
Where: src/kg/cli.py, src/kg/__main__.py, pyproject.toml, tests/test_cli.py.
Learned: implemented and pushed; the user must review and merge PR #13 (merge mode not chosen yet).

nodes.label: CLI on stdlib argparse with a single JSON envelope and fixed exit codes
nodes.description:
What: argparse (no Click/Typer); with --json the output is always one object {ok, command, result|error} on stdout; exit codes 0 OK, 1 validation, 2 usage, 3 internal; unexpected errors never show a traceback.
Why: no new dependencies (AGENTS.md rule 5) and machine-readable output for agents (RF-22, RNF-01, RNF-07).
Where: src/kg/cli.py.
Learned: argparse prints some messages in English ('show this help message'); translating them was left optional.

nodes.label: Exclude the root prototype scripts from ruff instead of fixing them
nodes.description:
What: graph.py, di_graph.py, tuto.py, the notebook etc. at the root are excluded from ruff.
Why: they are exploration scripts; new code lives in src/kg/.
Where: pyproject.toml ruff config.
Learned: ruff format also touched .agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md (only a blank line in an example).

nodes.label: Remove the example module src/kg/graphs.py and its test once real code exists
nodes.description:
What: delete the leftover build_tech_graph() example (taken from the prototype graph.py) and its test.
Why: placeholder from the initial structure; not part of kg.
Where: src/kg/graphs.py, tests/test_graphs.py.
Learned: needs the user's approval (no deletions without confirmation).
